newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Time Warner raised to buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Time Warner raised to buy.

text.p: Montgomery Securities analyst John Tinker raised the rating on Time Warner Inc to buy from hold, his office said.
-- raised the EBITDA -- earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization -- estimate to $4.988 billion from $4.985 billion for 1997, and to $5.592 billion from $5.473 billion for 1998.
-- raised the earnings estimate to loss $0.36 per share from loss $0.37 for 1997, and to profit $0.03 from loss $0.02 for 1998.
-- set 12-month price target of $66. Tinker had no target while the stock was rated hold.
-- shares gained 7/16 to 53-1/8 in early trade.

-- Tinker said, in a research note issued Wednesday, that the stock price should be boosted by the following: the company's improvement in EBITDA, which was up 15 percent in the first half; its intent to hold off on further acquisitions; and its focus on reducing debt.

-- said company's "mix of assets, particularly with cable television's emerging high-speed broadband network, recently endorsed by (Microsoft Corp's chairman) Bill Gates, makes Time Warner attractive."
-- Tinker forecasts nine percent revenue growth to $27.4 billion in 1998.
-- sees net debt of about $17.1 billion, or 30 percent of total capital -- market capitalization, plus preferred securities, plus net debt -- at end of 1997.
